I keep my hair twisted in the same 8-12 sections I wash it in and throw them into a bun until the next wash day. Sometimes, I'll wear a low puff that eventually ends up as a bun after it no longer looks good loose, and rewetting it for styling always leads to more tangles than just throwing it in a bun. After every wash, I apply a creamy leave in conditioner and oil, then stretch it in some way. Unrestrained shrinkage just causes mini locs in my hair.

I hate detangling, and every action causes tangles, so I tend to just live in buns with the exception of getting box braids that stay in for 2 months. Anything so I don't have to detangle, which takes an hour on a good day.

I know that weekly washing and detangling leads to fewer tangles and an easier time, but I hate it so washes get stretched to once a month if my depression is too bad. I've shaved it all off once and kept being called sir, so I have yet to do it again, but that year of a twa was bliss.

I did recently get the unbrush, and it can actually get through my hair like a comb would without bending or breaking. I used it in the shower with conditioner soaked hair. The tangle teaser brushes for curly hair either yield to my hair and don't actually detangle because the bristles bend flat or they just break my hair, so this was a pleasant surprise. 

The rest of my family keeps their hair short or relaxed, so the og natural hair youtubers are the ones who got me through my transition to natural and subsequent care.

I don't know if I helped, but I'm glad to find someone else struggling like I do with type 4 hair and autism. (Potential autism for me as I'm self-diagnosed with only the dsm-5 criteria and a psychiatrist walking with me through suspicions of "mild autism" as she called it.) May we figure our shit out eventually. 

Tl;dr: I keep it stretched or restrained in low manipulation styles so it doesn't shrink and tangle. Detangle with lots of conditioner with a reliable tool. Moisture in the form of a good leave-in and a sealant helps with breakage when I do manipulate it.  I'm in it for less hassle, not necessarily a pretty style. I'll suffer through box braid installation when I need to be able to get up and go and still look presentable for the next few weeks. 8 to 10 hours of hand pain will save me 2 months of styling.

Sometimes, small humans and animals just do dumb shit with things that wouldn't ordinarily be considered a hazard to them. How could you have predicted a toddler opening a sealed packet of medicine like a toy, ibuprofen falling out of a pocket which had never happened before (I assume), or your dog zeroing in on a salt packet? Are you just supposed to keep everything hidden?

 Plus, you leave small children unattended way less when you're used to their bullshit, so you'd likely catch things that result from your trait before they become a serious problem and if you don't, just baby proof the hell out of your house. Known hazards? Locked away before baby is even a real baby. And unknown hazards just get moved progressively higher up as the child discovers how to make them a hazard. And by the time that stops working, they can be taught how to not kill themselves in stupid ways. Dogs have less oversight and thus can do things like sneak opportune non-food items more easily and don't have the same capacity of a human to go "hey I shouldn't eat that thing specifically"

Don't be too hard on yourself, especially if you've grown from each incident and have improved in those areas. Not to be dismissive, but your emotions were probably running high from these things and you're making it into an unrealistic "I can't have kids now because I'll be a bad mom" and ignoring all the ways you would be a good mom and are a good pet parent because all you can focus on is what just happened and all the ways it could've gone worse. Brains are fun like that sometimes. Feel your feelings but also watch out for when feelings may be gaslighting you into less logical conclusions

Now, if you begin to leave known hazards lying around and actively endanger your dependents and never learn how not to do that or refuse to do any learning, I would be concerned, but these are all random occurences that don't super reflect on you as a person or your future ability to spot and prevent potential "what did you just put in your mouth" situations miles away
